chunks.text: N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025 KABC030138922019 Presented on : 23-02-2019 Registered on : 23-02-2019 Decided on : 01-08-2025 Duration : 6 years, 5 months, 6 days IN THE COURT OF THE 30TH ADDL.CHIEF JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE, BENGALURU Dated: This the 01st day of August-2025 :Present: Sri.Thimmaiah.G B.A. LLB. 30th ACJM, Bengaluru. C.C.No.4613/2019 Judgment U/s.355 of Cr.P.C. Date of Offence 12.04.2015 Complainant State by Puttenahalli Police Station, R/by. Learned Senior APP V/s. Accused Ranjith S/o.Rajendra, Aged about 25 years, R/at. No.38, Lakshmanapuri Slum, Behind PWD Office, Gandhinagar, Bengaluru City. Judgment 2 C.C.No.4613/2019 Offences U/s. 332, 341, 353, 504, 506 of IPC Plea Recorded on:10.12.2019 and accused is Pleaded not guilty. Examination U/sec., On 21.062025. 313 of Cr.P.C recorded on: Final Oder Accused is Acquitted. Date of Order 01.08.2025 N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025 Thimmaiah.G 30 ACJM, Bengaluru. th JUDGMENT The PSI of Puttenahalli Police Station has filed charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable U/s. 323, 341, 353, 504, 506 of IPC.

The brief facts of the prosecution case are as follows:- It is alleged that, the, Cw.1 is working as Traffic Head Constable at Puttenahalli Police Station, as per the instigation of Cw-10 he was on duty on 12.04.215 at 15 th Cross Junction, 33rd Main, JP Nagar 6th Phase, within the jurisdiction of JP Judgment 3 C.C.No.4613/2019 nagar Police Station, from 2.00pm in the afternoon till 1.00pm in the night, at that time, in spite of giving stop signal, the accused being driver of Pulsar two wheeler vehicle bearing No. KA-05-ET-5373 violated signal an moved further, when the same was questioned by the Cw1, the accused abused him in filthy language, further accused caught hold of the collar of the Cw.1 and wrongfully restrained him from moving further, Further, in furtherance of your common intention, the accused slapped Cw.1 on his face, punched on his stomach and pushed him down and caused hurt to a government servant and deter him from his duty. Further, the accused in furtherance of your common intention used criminal force on government servant and deter him to perform his duty and given life threat to the Cw.1 and thereby the accused has committed the above said alleged offences which are punishable U/s. 332, 341, 353, 504, 506 of IPC. After filing the charge sheet, cognizance taken for the offences punishable offences punishable U/s. 332, 341, 353, 504, 506 of IPC against the accused and accused was released on bail. Copy of the prosecution papers furnished to the accused as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. Heard before charge. Charge has been framed and read over to the accused language known to him wherein, he has denied the same and claim to be tried. Judgment 4 C.C.No.4613/2019

In order to secure the Cw.2,3,6 to 11 witnesses this court repeatedly issued Summons, NBW and Proclamation, even though the sufficient time given to the concerned police, they have failed to secure these witnesses. Moreover, this case is 07 years old one. Hence, the said witnesses are dropped after given sufficient opportunities to prosecution. In this regard this court relied on the following Hon'ble High Court, full bench Judgment of the Madras High Court, passed in The State ( N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025 Tamil Nadu) V/s Veerappan and Others, on 24 March 1980, AIR 1980 MAD260-ILR 3 MAD 245 where in it held as below: Of the two questions which have been referred to this Full Bench, the first one, namely, whether under Section 255(1) Cr. P. C., a Magistrate can acquit the accused if the prosecution fails to apply for the issue of summons to any witness and does not produce the witness for several hearings and does not serve summons on the witnesses despite having been granted sufficient opportunity to serve the summons or to produce the witnesses, is the one that directly arises for determination in these appeals. The second question which arises for determination by us incidentally is whether a Magistrate can acquit the accused under Section 248(1) Cr. P. C., if the prosecution does not apply for the issue of summons to any Judgment 5 C.C.No.4613/2019 of the witnesses and does not produce the witness for several hearings and does not serve the summons on the witnesses despite having been granted sufficient opportunities to serve the summons on the witnesses or to produce the witnesses.

In all these appeals, the learned Magistrate acquitted the accused under Section 255(1) Cr. P. C., on the ground that even though the cases had been posted for hearing on various dates and summons had been issued to the witnesses for all the hearings, the witnesses were not produced on any of the hearing dates and in spite of a notice issued that the case would be disposed of without examining the witnesses if they are not produced the prosecution did not choose to let in any evidence and as such the Magistrate found that the prosecution had no evidence to let in.

In State of Madh. Pra. v. Kaluthawar, 1972 Cri LJ 1639, a Division Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court observed as follows: "It was the duty of the prosecution to make necessary arrangements for the production of its witnesses.... The Police must always remember that it has got a duty to the court and they cannot just send a challan and think that the rest will be done by the court. When nobody appeared in t he court to inform what the reason was for non-appearance of the witnesses, the court could legitimately come to Judgment 6 C.C.No.4613/2019 the conclusion that the police was not very serious in prosecuting the offence which was a minor one. Under Section 245, the Magistrate can record an order of acquittal if there is no evidence to hold the accused guilty. If the prosecution did not take proper steps to produce the witnesses, or ask the court to give them time to do the same, or to issue fresh summons, the court was not bound to fix another date. The police has a duty towards the citizen. When the accused is brought before the court and the prosecuting department does not take any steps it will be an abuse of the process of the court to continue the trial. Bringing a person before the court accusing him of some offence is a serious matter and however petty the offence may be, the prosecuting department, must do its duty towards the accused as well as the court. When once the accused is challaned there is no privilege given to the police to remain absent". N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025

There are quite a number of decisions in which it had been held that an acquittal of the accused on the failure of the prosecution to produce the witnesses is not legal. (Vide State v. Kaliram Nandlal, ), the State of Mysore v. Ramu, 1973 Mad LJ (Crl.) 116: (1973 Cri LJ 1257) (Mys); State of Mysore v. Kalilulla Ahmed Sheriff. AIR 1971 Mys 60; Kanduri Misra v. Sabadev Kunda, (1962) 2 Cri LJ 295; State of Orissa v. Sibcharan Singh, ; State of Mysore v. Judgment 7 C.C.No.4613/2019 Somala, 1972 Mad LJ (Cri) 476: (1972 Cri LJ 1478) (Mys); State of Mysore v. Shanta, 1972 Mad LJ (Cri) 589 (Mys); State v. Nagappa, 1973 Cri LJ 548 (Mad); Public Prosecutor v. Sambangi Mudaliar, ; State of Kerala v. Kunhiaraman, 1964 Mad LJ (Cri) 330 (Ker); State of Mysore v. Narasimha Gowda, AIR 1965 Mys 167; State of Gujarat v. Thakorbhai Sukhabhai, , State of U.P. v. Ramjani, All LJ 1126; Lakshmiamma Kochukuttiamma v. Raman Pillai, AIR 1952 Trav-Co 268; State v. Madhavan Nair, 1959 Mad LJ (Cri) 633 (Ker); Emperor v. Varadarajulu Naidu, AIR 1932 Mad 25 (2); State of Kerala v. Desan Mary, 1960 Mad LJ (Cri) 378 (Ker); Kesar Singh v. State of Jammu and Kashmir, 1963-1 Cri LJ 765: (AIR 1963 J & K 23); R. K. V. Motors and Timbers Ltd. v. Regional Transport Authority, Trivandrum, ; K. K. Subbier v. K. M. S. Lakshmana Iyer, 1942 Mad WN (Cri) 64: (AIR 1942 Mad 452 (1)); State of Tripura v. Niranjan Deb Barma, 1973 Cri LJ 108 (Tripura); Apren Joseph v. State of Kerala, 1972 Mad LJ (Cri) 10: (1972 Cri LJ 1162) (Ker). As against these decisions, there are the following decisions in which it has been held that acquittal on the ground of non-production of witnesses by the prosecution was proper.

On the question as to whether the Magistrate can acquit an accused at all under Section 251A (11), Cr. P. C., if the prosecution Judgment 8 C.C.No.4613/2019 failed to produce their witnesses, a Division Bench of the Gujarat High Court observed in State of Gujarat v. Bava Bhadya (1962)'2 Cri LJ 537 (2), as follows: "Where a charge Is framed In a warrant case on police report, if owing to the failure of the prosecution to produce their witnesses and owing also to the failure of the prosecution to make full endeavour to serve the summonses according to the provisions contained in Sections 69, 70 and 71, Cr. P. C., 1890, there is no evidence before the Magistrate, the Magistrate can acquit the accused under Section 251A (11)." " In State of Karnataka v. Subramania Setti 1980 Mad LJ 138: (1980 CA LJ NOC 129), a Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court referring to the decisions in State of Mysore v. Narasimha Gowda (1964) 2 Mys LJ 241: (AIR 1965 Mys 167) and the State of Mysore v. Abdul Hameed Khan (1969) 1 Mys LJ 4: (1970 Cri LJ 112 (Mys)), observed that the real distinction between the two decisions is as to whether there was remissness and want of diligence on the part of the prosecuting agency in producing the witnesses before the Court and therefore the principle laid down in Abdul Hameed Khan's case applied to the facts of the case with which the Division Bench was concerned.

We may riots here that in Abdul Hameed Khan's case, it was found on the facts that the prosecution was not at all diligent as Judgment 9 C.C.No.4613/2019 the non-bailable warrants issued to the witnesses had neither been served nor returned to the court by the concerned police and it was therefore held that where the prosecution was not diligent in producing its witnesses and had failed to serve the bailable warrants on N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025 the witnesses and return the same the Magistrate would be justified in refusing to grant an adjournment and to proceed to acquit the accused on the material on record. We may note here that in State of Karnataka v. Subramania Setti 1980 MLJ 138 the Division Bench was dealing with a24. After carefully considering all the aforesaid decisions and the views expressed therein, we are of the view that if the prosecution had made an application for the issue of summons to its witnesses either under Section 242(2) or 254(2) of the Criminal Procedural Code it is the duty of the court to issue summons to the prosecution witnesses and to secure the witnesses by exercising all the powers given to it under the Criminal Procedure Code, as already indicated by us and if still the presence of the witnesses could not be secured and the prosecution also either on account of pronounced negligence or recalcitrance does not produce the witnesses after the Court had given it sufficient time and opportunities to do so, then the Court, being left with no other alternative would be justified in acquitting the accused for want of evidence to prove the Judgment 10 C.C.No.4613/2019 prosecution case, under Section 248, Cr. P. C., in the case of warrant cases instituted on a police report and under Section 255(1), Cr. P.

C. in summons cases, and we answer the two questions referred to us in the above terms. Hence, considering the present case on hand, the Cw.2,3,6 to 11 witnesses are dropped Further, the Cw.5 is given up as prayed by the learned Sr. APP. In order to prove the guilt of the accused persons, the prosecution has examined 04 witnesses as Pw.1 to Pw.4 and 03 documents are got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P3 and one uniform shirt is marked as Mo.1.

There are quite a number of decisions in which it had been held that an acquittal of the accused on the failure of the prosecution to produce the witnesses is not legal. (Vide State v. Kaliram Nandlal, ), the State of Mysore v. Ramu, 1973 Mad LJ (Crl.) 116: (1973 Cri LJ 1257) (Mys); State of Mysore v. Kalilulla Ahmed Sheriff. AIR 1971 Mys 60; Kanduri Misra v. Sabadev Kunda, (1962) 2 Cri LJ 295; State of Orissa v. Sibcharan Singh, ; State of Mysore v. Judgment 7 C.C.No.4613/2019 Somala, 1972 Mad LJ (Cri) 476: (1972 Cri LJ 1478) (Mys); State of Mysore v. Shanta, 1972 Mad LJ (Cri) 589 (Mys); State v. Nagappa, 1973 Cri LJ 548 (Mad); Public Prosecutor v. Sambangi Mudaliar, ; State of Kerala v. Kunhiaraman, 1964 Mad LJ (Cri) 330 (Ker); State of Mysore v. Narasimha Gowda, AIR 1965 Mys 167; State of Gujarat v. Thakorbhai Sukhabhai, , State of U.P. v. Ramjani, All LJ 1126; Lakshmiamma Kochukuttiamma v. Raman Pillai, AIR 1952 Trav-Co 268; State v. Madhavan Nair, 1959 Mad LJ (Cri) 633 (Ker); Emperor v. Varadarajulu Naidu, AIR 1932 Mad 25 (2); State of Kerala v. Desan Mary, 1960 Mad LJ (Cri) 378 (Ker); Kesar Singh v. State of Jammu and Kashmir, 1963-1 Cri LJ 765: (AIR 1963 J & K 23); R. K. V. Motors and Timbers Ltd. v. Regional Transport Authority, Trivandrum, ; K. K. Subbier v. K. M. S. Lakshmana Iyer, 1942 Mad WN (Cri) 64: (AIR 1942 Mad 452 (1)); State of Tripura v. Niranjan Deb Barma, 1973 Cri LJ 108 (Tripura); Apren Joseph v. State of Kerala, 1972 Mad LJ (Cri) 10: (1972 Cri LJ 1162) (Ker). As against these decisions, there are the following decisions in which it has been held that acquittal on the ground of non-production of witnesses by the prosecution was proper.

Thereafter examination of the accused persons under Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is recorded, then the accused persons denied the incriminating evidence in the prosecution case and not chosen to lead their side evidence. No documents are got marked on their behalf. Heard both sides and perused the evidence available on record. Upon hearing arguments advanced from both sides and on perusal of materials placed on record, following points arise for consideration: Judgment 11 C.C.No.4613/2019 POINTS Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the Cw.1 is working as Traffic Head Constable at Puttenahalli Police Station, as per the instigation of Cw-10 he was on duty on 215 at 15th Cross Junction, 33rd Main, JP Nagar 6th Phase, within the jurisdiction of JP nagar Police Station, from 2.00pm in the afternoon till 1.00pm in the night, at that time, in spite of giving stop signal, the accused being driver of Pulsar two wheeler vehicle bearing No. KA-05-ET-5373 violated signal an moved N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025 further, when the same was questioned by the Cw1, the accused abused him in filthy language, and thereby committed an offence punishable U/sec.,504 of IPC? Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, further the accused caught hold of the collar of the Cw.1 and wrongfully illegally restrained him from moving forward and thereby committed an offence punishable U/sec.,341 of IPC? Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, further, the accused slapped Cw.1 on his face, punched on his stomach and pushed him Judgment 12 C.C.No.4613/2019 down and caused hurt to a government servant and deter him from his duty and thereby committed an offence punishable U/sec.,332 of IPC?

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, further, the accused obstructed the government servant duty and thereby committed an offence punishable U/sec.,353 of IPC? Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, further, the accused given life threat to the Cw.1 and thereby committed an offence punishable U/sec.,506 of IPC? What order.? My findings to the above points are: Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : In the Negative Point No.3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : In the Negative Point No.5 : In the Negative Point No.6 : As per final order for the following. REASONS Judgment 13 C.C.No.4613/2019 POINTS NO.1 TO 5: These points are inter connected to each other and have taken for discussion in common to avoid repetition of the facts and evidence. Further, I am of the opinion that, I need not repeat the entire case of the complaint here also, since I have already narrated the same at the inception of this judgment. N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025

The Cw.1 Srinivas, who is examined as Pw.1 and complainant/injured witness to the case, he has deposed in his evidence before the court that, On 12-4-2015, he was posted on duty on 33rd Main Road from 2:00 PM to 10:00 PM to control traffic. At 5:35 PM, there was a lot of traffic. He was signaling to control traffic. At that time, two people from 33rd Main Road came towards 15th Cross on a Pulsar bike. At that time, he instructed the vehicles coming from 33rd Road to stop and let the vehicles moving from east to west go. The rider on the back of the Pulsar bike shouted at him to leave quickly, abused him in filthy language and jumped off the bike, grabbed his collar and assaulted him on the cheek and punched on his stomach. The public came and caught hold the accused, when he asked him his name, he found out that it was Ranjit. When the public caught the accused, the accused threatened him, later he informed the same to the control room over the phone and wireless. Later, the JP Nagar Hoysala came and took the accused away. Later, he went to the Judgment 14 C.C.No.4613/2019 police station and filed a complaint and due to the accused's behavior obstructed the Cw.1's duty as a public servant. Further, the learned counsel for the accused had cross examined the said witness, where in he stated that, the accused was a pillion rider on the bike, further he did not take any treatment on the day of incident, he do not anybody name who was present in the crowed, he do not know the names of persons who put their signatures on spot mahazar and there is no CCTV in the incident spot and further denied the rest of the suggestions put by the learned counsel for the accused.

I have carefully perused the complaint Ex.P1 given by the complainant, where in he written that, there was no such injuries to take treatment in the hospital and further he stated the that, the pillen rider ie., accused had drink the alcohol, further in his cross examination he admitted that, he do know the spot mahazar witnesses name. Further, material object ie., uniform of the Cw.1 is not produced before the court and did not marked the same whether it was torned or not as alleged by him. As such, there is contradiction in his evidence. Under such, circumstances, the court can not consider his evidence as proved one with cogent and believable evidence to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

The Cw.4 Venkatesh, who is examined as Pw.2 and incident witness to the case, he has deposed in his evidence Judgment 15 C.C.No.4613/2019 before the court that, On 12-04-2015, when he reported for duty at the police station, the station officer assigned him and Cw-5 to patrol in a Hoysala vehicle. Accordingly, we received information from the control room at 06:00 PM that there was quarrel at 6th stage, 15th cross, 33rd main road of JP Nagar. They should go there immediately. Accordingly, when we went there, the accused grabbed Cw-1 by the clothes, abused him in filthy language and slapped him on his face and forehead, and obstructed his duty. The public caught hold of the accused. Later, we took him into our custody and when we asked him his name, he told it is Ranjit. Later, we produced him before our station officer Cw.11. N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025 Further, the learned counsel for the accused had cross examined the said witness, where in he stated that, he did mentioned in the station dairy that, on the date of incident he was deputed to Hoysala duty, further he did not mentioned in his statement, that at what time he bought the accused to police station and further denied the rest of the suggestions put by the learned counsel for the accused.

The Cw.12 Smt. Renuka G.M, who is examined as Pw.3 and IO in this case, she has deposed in her evidence before the court that, On 12.04.2015, she had received the case file from Cw-11 and continued the investigation. Then, she had conducted the panchnama in the presence of pancha's Judgment 16 C.C.No.4613/2019 at the same place shown by Cw-1 from 07-30 to 08-15. Then, on the same day, she had conducted the seizure panchanama in the presence of pancha's and seized the uniform of the Cw.1 and included it in the police station P.F.No. No. 85/2015. Then, on the same day, she had recorded the statements of Cw-2 to 5. Then, since she was transferred, the Cw-13 had taken over the further investigation. Further, the learned counsel for the accused had cross examined the said witness, where in she stated that, the incident place is traffic signal and she had not investigate whether, on the incident spot their was a CCTV camera or not, further she did not enquired that, the accused was drunk the alcohol or not at the time of incident, further the seized Uniform, Mo.1 it is mentioned in the PF that, the uniform shirt button was torned but, the same is not mentioned in the complaint Ex.P1, further, she had not taken the signatures wrote the Ex.P2 Spot Panchana and Ex.P3 Seizure Panchanama and further denied the rest of the suggestions put by the learned counsel for the accused.

The Cw.13 Sri.Raghu Naik, who is examined as Pw.4 and IO in this case, he has deposed in his evidence before the court that, On 14.07.2018, he had received the case file from the JP Nagar Police Station, examined it and continued the investigation. Later, after examining the case file, the Judgment 17 C.C.No.4613/2019 investigation has already been completed and since the charges against the accused have been prima facie proven, he had submitted the final report to the Honorable Court. It is the paramount duty of the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt. Unless the guilt is established beyond all reasonable doubt, the accused can not be held guilty of the alleged offenses. Further, in order to secure the Cw.2,3,6 to 11 witnesses respectively this court so many times issued summons and proclamation. In spite of the sufficient time given to the police, they have failed to secure these witnesses. Hence, Cw.2,3, 6 to 11 are dropped after given sufficient time. In which Cw.3 and 9 are eye witnesses, but prosecution did not secure the same in order to prove the case. N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025

In the present case material witness such as i.e Pw.1 has not proved one regarding the prosecution case with regard to the Ex.P1 & 2 complaint and spot mahazar. Further police officials evidence are not proved with cogent and believable evidence to prove the guilt of the accused wherein they deposed as per their investigation in order to obtain the material object ie., torned uniform of Pw.1 and in the interest of their department and there is a lacuna in their investigation. Further, material object ie., Uniform of the Cw.1 Judgment 18 C.C.No.4613/2019 is did not produced before the court and it did not marked the same, in the absence of the same, court can not be come to the conclusion that, the said Uniform was torned or not, in the absence of the same, prosecution has failed to prove the case with cogent and necessary evidence. Moreover, in the absence of the independent and eye witness, the court can not relay on the police officials evidence and their evidence is not helpful to the prosecution to prove their case as cogent evidence with chain link . Under such circumstances, it is difficult to believe the version of the the Pw.1 to 4 regarding the offence committed by the accused as alleged by the Pw.1 in Ex.P1. As such the case against the accused is certainly would be entitled to benefit of the doubt. Regarding this this court, relied on the following Judgment. On this point held in, (2016) 10 SCC 519 - AIR 2016 SC 4581 in para 56, Hon'ble Apex held thus hereunder: ''56. It is a trite proposition of law, that suspicion however grave, it cannot take the place of proof and that the prosecution in order to succeed on a criminal charge cannot afford to lodge its case in the realm of ''may be true''' but has to essentially elevate it to the grade of ''must be true''.

In a criminal prosecution, the court has a duty to ensure that mere conjectures or suspicion do not take the place of legal proof and in a situation Judgment 19 C.C.No.4613/2019 where a reasonable doubt is entertained in the backdrop of the evidence available, to prevent miscarriage of justice, benefit of doubt is to be extended to the accused. Such a doubt essentially has to be reasonable and not imaginary, fanciful, intangible or non-existent but as entertainable by an impartial, prudent and analytical mind, judged on the touchstone of reason and common sense. It is also a primary postulation in criminal jurisprudence that if two views are possible on the evidence available one pointing to the guilt of the accused and the other to his innocence, the one favourable to the accused ought to be adopted.''

Further, in order to secure the Cw.2,3,6 to 11 witnesses respectively this court so many times issued summons and proclamation. In spite of the sufficient time given to the police, they have failed to secure these witnesses. Hence, Cw.2,3, 6 to 11 are dropped after given sufficient time. In which Cw.3 and 9 are eye witnesses, but prosecution did not secure the same in order to prove the case. N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025 In the present case, it is important to note that the material witness and the IO witnesses have not proved the alleged commission of the offences by the accused with corroborative evidence. As such the accused has certainly would be entitled to benefit of the doubt, since no corroborative evidence of the witnesses against the accused to prove the prosecution case. Hence, the accused is entitled to the benefit of the reasonable doubt. By considering all these aspects the prosecution utterly failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt. Therefore, I answer to the Point No.1 to 5 in the Negative. N Srinivas, Hc-4729 vs Ranjith on 1 August, 2025 Judgment 20 C.C.No.4613/2019

POINT NO.6: In view of the above findings on Point No.1 to 5, I proceed to pass the following: : ORDER : The Powers Conferred Upon me U/Sec. 248(1) of Cr.P.C. The Accused is hereby Acquitted for the alleged offences punishable U/sec.,332, 324, 353, 504, 506 of IPC. The bail bond of Accused and surety extended for further 6 months in order to comply Sec.437A of Cr.P.C. Thereafter, this bail bond automatically stands cancelled. The property seized by the IO in P.F.No.85/2015, One Uniform Shirt is being worthless, is hereby ordered to be destroy the same, after the appeal period is over, in accordance with law.
